title: THE WAITING OF LAST MEETING
summary: A story of love, memories, separation and an unfinished wait.
body:
**Chapter 4 — When Care Slowly Became Love**

There was a time when our conversations were just simple and ordinary. We talked about studies, friends, family, food and many other little things. Neither of us knew exactly where these conversations were taking us. We never planned to become so close. It just happened naturally, one conversation at a time.

As the days passed, I started noticing something different about her. She was becoming more caring towards me, and perhaps I was becoming the same towards her. Whenever I went to work, she would sometimes ask when I would be coming back. Even during my evening and night shifts, she wanted to know how things were going and when I would return. Those little questions slowly became meaningful to me.

My working hours were usually from around five in the evening until night. After spending hours at work, I would often call her. Sometimes she would ask, "When will you come back?" or "How was your day?" These were very simple questions, but they made me feel that someone was interested in the little details of my everyday life.

Slowly, we started sharing almost everything about our days. If something happened at work, I would tell her. If something happened in her life, she would share it with me. We talked about what we had done throughout the day, what we had eaten, what was happening around us and even the smallest things that might not have mattered to anyone else. Our conversations became a natural part of our daily routine.

I also started telling her more about my family, my life and the things that were important to me. She shared her own experiences, too. We were not just talking to pass the time anymore; we were gradually becoming part of each other's everyday lives. Without even realising it, we had started caring about how the other person was doing.

There were also little things that made our conversations special. I knew that she liked momos and South Indian food. Sometimes, she would ask me to order something for her, and I would happily arrange it. These small moments might seem ordinary to someone else, but they became beautiful memories for me. It was never about the food itself; it was about those little ways we started looking after each other.

One thing about her always stayed in my heart. She never wanted to question me about my past relationships. She had told me that whatever had happened before we met belonged to the past. She wanted us to enjoy the present and talk about our future rather than keep asking questions about yesterday. From the beginning of our relationship until the end, she never questioned me about my former girlfriends. That attitude made me respect her even more. I felt that I had met someone who understood relationships in a different way.

And somewhere between those late-night conversations, little questions about our days, sharing family stories and caring for each other, something beautiful began to happen. We started talking about feelings, and our conversations slowly became more affectionate. Neither of us had planned that moment. We didn't even realise exactly when our friendship had started turning into something deeper. One day, I simply looked back and understood that we had fallen in love.

Perhaps that is how some of the most meaningful relationships begin—not with a promise, not with a plan, but with two people slowly becoming a part of each other's everyday lives.
